title: A training week in Osaka for an athlete who asks for Italian lunches and dinners: does their request beat the country?
message: Could you plan my meals for next week, {Mon} to {Sun}?
Tue: 1h10 run with 5 x 5 min at threshold
Thu: 50 min easy run with 6 strides
I weigh 64 kg and live in Osaka, Japan. No restrictions. The fridge is empty.
I love Italian food, so please make all my lunches and dinners Italian dishes. Ordinary Japanese breakfasts are fine.
That's everything — please go ahead and make the plan.

judge.question: Is every lunch and dinner in the plan an Italian dish as the athlete asked, including the Italian-style dishes people outside Italy cook as Italian food, and none of them Japanese or from another cuisine? Name any that is not.
Is every breakfast in the plan one an ordinary household in Japan would make on a weekday? Name any that would be unusual there.
Does the reply avoid telling the athlete that their request for Italian lunches and dinners was set aside, cut back or replaced with Japanese food? Answer yes if it says nothing of the kind.
Does every supermarket or shop chain the plan or the reply names trade in Japan? Answer yes if none is named.
Could every item on the shopping list be bought in an ordinary supermarket in Osaka, without a specialist import shop? Name any that could not.
